title: Is it possible to make enemy resistant to special effect?

posts.author: cepter
posts.body:
I have made an actor skill which makes enemy escape if succeed. Thats the only purpose of the skill.
Database -> Skills and from there I have selected the skill which has only one effect typed as "Special effect" content: "Escape"
Is it possible to make enemy resistant to that skill? I have tried everything I can come up with. I tried to swich damage type from none to any from the list, so then I can change the element. Then I made the enemy resistant to that element, but it does not work.
One possibility is that you make the enemy appear on certain locations on the map via event, and not checking the "can escape" box. Then you cannot even perform the attack. But I think it would be much better, if the skill can be performed and the enemy is resistant.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
Not by default and not directly
what you can do is install a plugin that allows for skill or target conditions and use javascript to program an exception by notetag.
There are several such plugins that would allow that, for example from yanfly and tsukihime (iirc).
do you have any of those plugins already?

posts.author: caethyril
Andar
posts.body:
addendum:
there is a way of making something like you want by default, I just thought of it
1) make a state that seals that specific skill
2) in the troop for the boss enemy, make a troop event on turn 0 that applies that state to every actor
doing it this way blocks the skill for that fight, which means against every enemy in that troop if there is more than the boss
but it is the only way to do this with selective enemies, and even then it's for the entire troop instead of a specific enemy.

caethyril said:
Target effects apply whenever the action hits, regardless of damage.
Depending on exactly what you want to do, one of these workarounds might be OK:
You could set the skill's
Success
rate to, say, 70%. That would give it a constant 30% chance of failing on
any
target.
You could set the skill's
Hit Type
to Physical or Magical, and give the enemy high Evasion/Reflection for that hit type to reduce the hit chance for all actions of that type.
Otherwise, like Andar says, you'd want a suitable plugin.

Every skill/item checks for hit/miss on each applicable target. As I said, per-target effects (like Escape) only apply to targets that have been hit.

damage
type/element, not the
hit
type:
cepter said:
I tried to swich damage type from none to any from the list, so then I can change the element. Then I made the enemy resistant to that element, but it does not work.
Click to expand...
Element affects damage; hit type affects hit/evasion checks. Hit types are:
Certain Hit = always hit (and ignore the target's state/debuff rates);
Physical Attack = checks user's Hit Rate and target's Evasion;
Magical Attack = checks target's Magic Evasion (and Magic Reflection).
By contrast, damage elements can be defined by you, on the Types tab in the database.

OK, if it's for specific enemies then you'll either want:
Something like Andar suggested: a troop event with "Condition = Turn 0" that adds a state with a Seal Skill trait to everyone, and set the state to auto-remove on battle end.
...or an appropriate plugin~

Thank you for the answer. So this solution almost worked:
When the enemy appears there is a turn 0 event: "Change Skill : Actor, - Skill" then another event on same page "Change Skill : Actor, + Skill"
First it removes the original skill, then it adds new skill which has same name as the original, but this time it has 0% succession rate.
Then I added new event page for the same enemy and reversed that recipe for turn end...but in this case it reverses also everything after first attempt...still learning...
EDIT vol 238:
I´m being very frustrated but this seems to work after one test:
On troops there is only one event page with 0 event: "Change Skill : Actor, - Skill" and "Change Skill : Actor, + Skill" - as I wrote earlier to this, the original skill is now replaced with new skill which has same name as the original skill, but this new skill has 0% succession rate.
Then after battle there is parallel event on the map which reverses that recipe...seems to work.
FINAL EDIT:
Phew...it works flawlessly
